{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the belly line, stroke 2, the full lower curve of the fish body. It runs from the nose to the tail stem and is one of the two main outline strokes the picture depends on. Over the session I laid about 50 dominoes on it and re-stood the ones that were knocked down. I also put in the final joins from the start row into the belly line near the end.

Execution: I finished the belly line early, around the three-minute mark, so the tail forks could lay themselves onto it. I then spent my time on the nose join, where the fall has to split into the top and belly lines. I inspected that area closely several times to find where the chain stalled. I bridged gaps, re-seated a tight domino after Omar pointed it out, and kept working the join until time was called.

Collaboration: I kept my hands off the nose when Jack was rebuilding it, so we wouldn't undo each other's work. When Hana took the top bridge I took the belly side, so we weren't nudging the same dominoes. I backed Hana's suggestion to start at the nose and asked for the lines to flatten gently into the tail stem. I also kept the table updated on what I was touching, which helped Jack, Hana and Omar plan around me.

Leadership: I kept the table focused on the one problem that mattered, the nose join, and pushed for a dry run once the joins were in. I set clear ownership (belly for me, top bridge for Hana) and called for hands-off at the end so nothing got bumped before the push. I took the belly line and the nose join as my responsibility from the start and stayed on them to the end.", "my_share_percent": 30}
